title: ‘We sound more like Labour’: Burnham brings good vibes to Liverpool
gist: Kathryn Schoon reports that Andy Burnham's first Labour conference speech as prime minister in Liverpool lifted party morale and unified the left, with MPs and activists saying Labour finally 'sounds like Labour'. His big promises — scrapping the pensions triple lock for a national care service, electoral reform, leasehold reform — face their first test at the 28 October Autumn Budget.

insights.claim: Labour members at the Liverpool conference reported a much better mood than the previous year, with Keir Starmer's premiership already feeling a distant memory and leaving little prominent legacy despite his large majority.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: Leadership change has reset Labour's internal cohesion, reducing near-term risk of party infighting.
insights.locator: Ahead of the prime minister’s speech

insights.claim: Burnham has been criticised during his first 10 weeks in office for prioritising style over substance and 'vibes', but Schoon argues the conference sentiment went beyond vibes to a tangible sense of possible change.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: Political momentum may support Labour polling recovery, but substance is unproven.

insights.claim: Burnham's enthusiasm and ability to connect draw comparisons with New York mayor Zohran Mamdani; South Yorkshire mayor Oliver Coppard credits Burnham's time as Manchester mayor for a long-term, place-based way of doing politics.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: Mayoral-style, place-focused governance may shape policy toward regional devolution.
insights.quote: You do your politics differently as a mayor

insights.claim: Self-described 'hardcore left' MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy said even she is willing to give Burnham a chance, crediting him with fixing a serious communication problem in the Parliamentary Labour Party, while warning the proof will be in the pudding.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: Reduced left-wing rebellion risk improves the government's ability to pass legislation.
insights.quote: he just said Labour things in a Labour way and now we sound more like Labour
insights.locator: Despite considering herself on the “hardcore left”

insights.claim: Burnham speaks fluently about neoliberalism and political economy, and What's Left? podcast host Freddie Feltham claimed his leadership underlies polling suggesting most Green and Liberal Democrat voters would be open to backing Labour depending on its direction.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: A leftward rhetorical shift could consolidate the centre-left vote, implying more interventionist economic policy.
insights.locator: Burnham speaks about concepts like neoliberalism

insights.claim: Compass chair Neal Lawson says Burnham can appeal both to 'Reform-curious' working-class voters and those drawn to the Greens and Lib Dems, and credits Green pressure for stopping Labour's drift right; he warns that without bolder left politics, the far right will own radical politics.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: Pressure from the left is pushing Labour toward more radical economic policy — relevant to UK fiscal and regulatory outlook.
insights.quote: if it doesn’t, it’ll be the far-right that are doing the radical, bolder politics
insights.locator: Neal Lawson, the co-founder and chair

insights.claim: Lawson cites Ed Miliband's recent sanctions on Israeli settlements in the West Bank as part of Labour's appeal to left-leaning voters.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: UK foreign policy is tilting toward tougher measures on Israeli settlements.
insights.locator: Neal Lawson, the co-founder and chair

insights.claim: Lawson questions whether Burnham can narrate his premiership while also delivering big transformative shifts in government.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: Execution risk remains the key uncertainty for the new government.
insights.quote: He’s narrating his own premiership, but can he do that at the same time as he does the big shift stuff as well?
insights.locator: Echoing both an appreciation and scepticism

insights.claim: Burnham's leader's speech pledged scrapping the pensions triple lock to create a 'national care service', electoral reform and leasehold reform, and his government's first Autumn Budget on 28 October will be the next test.
insights.speaker: Kathryn Schoon
insights.so_what: The 28 October Budget is the key catalyst for gilts and UK fiscal credibility under the new PM.
insights.locator: Following his announcements in his leader’s speech
